You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hotspot Sniper｜2026.09.08  Main theme: Post-Labor Day reopen｜Astra compute rebound · HBM capacity ramp · Foldable iPhone event · Cybercab probe

TEXT:
1. OpenAI GPT -6 Astra rolls out, memory and compute priced first
GPT-6 Astra launched on Sept. 3–4 and is rolling out to Plus/Pro/Enterprise users plus the API, Azure, and AWS Bedrock. OpenAI called it its largest pretraining run to date, with more than 100,000 GPUs at the Texas Stargate site; Greg Brockman publicly linked the model to an “ AGI era ,” highlighting computer use, coding, and cybersecurity. Korean shares front-ran the theme on Monday: KOSPI closed +4.61%, with Samsung and SK hynix surging, after the PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 3.38% on Friday.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MU, SNDK, NVDA, MSFT; Key catalyst: Astra usage confirming training/inference load; watch whether memory and GPU turnover extends Friday’s split tape.
2. Micron targets ~100k HBM wafers/month by year-end for NVIDIA Vera Rubin
Industry sources cited by Korean media and TrendForce say Micron plans to lift HBM monthly capacity from about 40k–50k wafers last year to ~100k by year-end, adding up to ~60k wafers/month. 12-hi HBM4’s share could rise from 20%–30% early this year to ~50%, tied to NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform. On Friday MU rose about 6.1% and SanDisk (SNDK) about 11.9%, making memory one of the few pockets that held up against the rate-hike tape.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MU, SNDK, NVDA; Key catalyst: HBM4 ramp and Rubin supply cadence; watch MU/SNDK beta versus the tape.
3. Apple “Surprise and Shine” tomorrow: Ternus’ first foldable showcase
Apple has confirmed its fall event on Sept. 9 at 10:00 a.m. PT. New CEO John Ternus (took over Sept. 1) will host for the first time. Focus is the first foldable iPhone (rumored iPhone Ultra/Fold, passport-sized, possibly $2,000+) plus iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max ; the standard iPhone 18 may slip to spring 2027. AAPL fell about 2.51% on Friday; the event window opens from tonight’s pre-market.
🎯 Beneficiaries: AAPL; Key catalyst: Sept. 9 pricing, foldable specs, and supply-chain commentary; volatility clusters around the keynote.
4. Tesla Cybercab goes commercial, NHTSA opens a probe the same week
Tesla has started limited paid Cybercab rides in Austin via the Robotaxi app—two-seater, no steering wheel, no pedals. NHTSA opened an audit query hours after launch to review Tesla’s self-certification against FMVSS and the decision not to seek a Part 555 exemption of the type Zoox used. TSLA closed about -5.92% on Friday as the robotaxi/robotics story collided with regulatory risk.
🎯 Beneficiaries: TSLA; Key catalyst: NHTSA audit updates and Austin fleet scale; headline-driven more than fundamental.
5. Meta “Iris” enters the September production window; 14GW narrative returns
A Reuters-reviewed internal memo said Meta’s custom data-center chip Iris (designed with Broadcom, built by TSMC) is slated to enter manufacturing in September after a ~6-week test with no major issues. Compute targets: ~7GW in 2026, doubling to 14GW in 2027, with AI infrastructure spend up to about $145bn this year, plus long-term deals for Samsung memory and SanDisk flash. The story was recirculated into the holiday weekend and helped chip names hold up better than software.
🎯 Beneficiaries: META, AVGO, TSM, SNDK; Key catalyst: Iris production timing and capex validation; watch hyperscaler commentary after the reopen.
6. Macro/events: reopen day + hike-data week + Canada tariffs + Oracle earnings
U.S. cash equities were closed Monday for Labor Day; today is the first full session. Friday’s payrolls printed +162k, well above forecasts, unemployment 4.1%; CME FedWatch put September hike odds near 58%–63%. This week: PPI (Sept. 10), CPI (Sept. 11), FOMC (Sept. 16). Canada’s 15%/25%/50% counter-tariffs on about $20–27.6bn of U.S. goods took effect 12:01 a.m. Sept. 8, covering steel, appliances, electronics and more. Oracle reports FY27 Q1 after the close on Sept. 10; focus is OCI and capex.
🎯 Beneficiaries: ORCL; Key catalyst: rate-path repricing versus cloud capex guidance; start with futures and Treasury yields.
Trading note: The first post-holiday session pits a “hike-trade vs. valuations” tape against event pricing in Astra/HBM/foldables/custom silicon. Friday’s flow already favored memory and semis over high-multiple software and TSLA. Watch Treasury yields, SOX, and MU/SNDK volume; size risk off VIX and overnight futures.
U.S. stocks have been more volatile lately. This is for information only and is not investment advice.
